newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian budget to cut deficit to 2.9 percent GDP.
newsitem.headline: Belgian budget to cut deficit to 2.9 percent GDP.

text.p: The Belgian government is to take measures in the 1997 budget which will enable it to cut the ratio of the country's budget deficit to gross domestic product to 2.9 percent, a government statement said on Tuesday.
"Thanks to this budget, our country will comply with the Maastricht treaty criteria for monetary union," Prime minister Jean-Luc Dehaene told parliament.
The budget statement said the deficit would be three percent of GDP in 1996.
The government also aimed to cut the country's public debt by 370 billion francs ($11.8 billion) by the end of next year.
This would be achieved through a series of measures which include a 222 billion franc reduction of foreign currency debt by using central bank capital gains on past gold sales.

The measures would come into effect rapidly due to the extended powers that parliament granted to the government in July, empowering it to take all necessary actions without prior parliamentary consent, the government statement said.
The 370 billion francs package should reduce Belgium's public debt as a percentage of gross domestic product to 127.0 percent in 1997 from 130.4 in 1996 and 137.0 percent in 1993.
"Thus the debt ratio will have fallen by 10 percent in a four-year period," Dehaene said.
The budget will contain a total 80 billion francs austerity package, compared with 1996's set of measures worth more than 110 billion francs. ($1=31.36 Belgian Franc)
